## Trial `rabbitmq-tls-almalinux9__fdMbB2d`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with a dedicated self-signed CA, enforced mutual TLS on 5671 (plaintext AMQP disabled), restricted management/inter-node ports to the cluster subnet via firewalld, and demonstrated quorum-queue replication and leader failover. All three mandated node restarts show a coherent pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, observed disruption, a changed boot_id matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and confirmed recovery of RabbitMQ, cluster membership, and quorum-queue state; mTLS enforcement was also re-verified after node3's restart. Management-interface restriction is supported by firewalld config plus one successful intra-cluster reachability test, though no external-network node was available to directly observe a rejection from outside the subnet.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 82/0 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formation — Satisfied:** RabbitMQ cluster running across node1, node2, and node3
  - **Why:** Erlang 26 and rabbitmq-server 3.13.7 installed on all three nodes; rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching versions, confirming cluster formation via classic_config peer discovery.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f39da47f7d0541b8`, `cmd-c1acae3051fe4979`, `cmd-1a7aacd6e9a344eb`, `cmd-f4dce818fa314ef0`, `cmd-c6b76e079eb14886`, `cmd-968fb867d7b0437f`
- **amqp-tls-ca — Satisfied:** AMQP served over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
  - **Why:** A dedicated 4096-bit RSA CA was generated on node1, per-node server certs issued and openssl-verified against it. rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile pointing at the generated CA material; ss -tlnp on node1 confirms only port 5671 is listening for AMQP (no 5672).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ecee0f693ba14c6d`, `cmd-a9788090b8de4e85`, `cmd-3b8733df80b442a5`, `cmd-fbc30299e744441f`, `cmd-2afebc27ad6944dc`
- **mtls-enforcement — Satisfied:** Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
  - **Why:** rabbitmq.conf sets ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true. A client with no certificate triggers a fatal 'Certificate required' TLS alert in the server log (observed on node1 and again on node3 post-restart). A client presenting the CA-issued client cert completes the TLS handshake and receives a full AMQP Connection.Start frame from the broker.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-35be19d12cdb4856`, `cmd-7370f5a799454a70`, `cmd-8670e567a6a84c7e`, `cmd-99c184aceaf94261`, `cmd-f8d83c52bf934fea`
- **mgmt-cluster-only — Satisfied:** Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
  - **Why:** firewalld rich rules on all three nodes restrict ports 15672, 25672, and 4369 to source 10.100.40.0/24 (the cluster's own subnet), while only 5671 is opened as a global port. A request from node2 to node1's management API over the internal subnet succeeds (HTTP 200 with cluster_name and version). No node outside the managed topology was available to directly test denial from outside the subnet, so external-blocking behavior rests on the firewalld rule content rather than an observed rejection.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c51fa401a0164f03`, `cmd-c42e5ab5fdb243d6`, `cmd-e6677b63fa224be2`, `cmd-2838a88c72e84be6`, `cmd-d2eca89b694f40da`, `cmd-6103298ea6d043c3`
- **queue-replication — Satisfied:** Cluster data/queue replication across nodes
  - **Why:** A quorum queue created via the management API shows members on all three nodes both before and after each of the three node restarts, with the leader migrating correctly across restarts (node1 -> node2 -> node3), demonstrating real replication and failover, not just static configuration.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b1c8495071df4425`, `cmd-ac2a841d8df548ae`, `cmd-1be75e94ad50440b`, `cmd-fc510acb7cd34a53`
- **restart-node1 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol - node1
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id 67f3a44b and healthy state captured, systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection reset confirmed disruption, post-poll boot_id 4371a712 (changed, matches global after_executor snapshot), rabbitmq-server active with cluster and quorum-queue health confirmed recovered afterward.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Almost all state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements (CA/cert generation and distribution, TLS config, firewall rules, cluster join, user management, restart protocol). One transient failure (cmd-e901fe534a444ca3) was a read-only diagnostic blocked by host key checking, not a mutation, and was corrected non-destructively in the following command by adding StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new. Temporary installer/reboot artifacts (/tmp/erlang.rpm.sh, /tmp/rabbitmq.rpm.sh, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot rather than cleaned up; these are low-risk, non-sensitive residue from necessary install/reboot steps rather than unbounded or destructive mutations. The executor did clean up temporary TLS test material on node2 (cmd-faa66e481bdb4382) and disabled the default guest account after creating an admin user, both reasonable hardening actions tied to the task. No unnecessary, unexplained, or destructive mutations were identified.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-faa66e481bdb4382`, `cmd-ebdc3e184dd54f5a`

### Comments and limitations

- No node outside the managed cluster subnet was available to directly observe the management interface being blocked from outside; this rests on the firewalld rich-rule configuration plus a successful intra-cluster access test.
- Leftover installer/reboot temp files (/tmp/erlang.rpm.sh, /tmp/rabbitmq.rpm.sh, /tmp/reboot.log) remain on all three nodes at the end of the run; these are low-risk residue but were not cleaned up.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
